title: Embed a thin skin strip in paraffin: press it flat with forceps while the other hand slides the mould onto the cold spot
instruction: Embed the skin strip that lies in the paraffin-filled mould on the warm plate. With the warm forceps, move it to the middle of the mould and press it flat, inked face down. Keep it pressed with the forceps while the other hand slides the mould across onto the cold spot, and keep pressing until the wax at the bottom has set. Then put the forceps back in their well and move both hands away.
context: Laboratory research automation: paraffin embedding is the routine hand step between tissue processing and sectioning in histology labs, research and clinical, done at an embedding station with warm forceps. Thin specimens such as skin curl; the technician holds them flat against the bottom of the metal mould with forceps until the paraffin has cooled (US patent 8,329,120, which also notes how hard it is to lift the forceps away without dislodging the piece). A strip that sets curled is sectioned at an angle: its sections miss part of the cut face, or the block is re-melted and embedded again. The standard sequence (ARUP Laboratories, histology terms): lay the piece cut face down in the middle, press it flat, move the mould onto the cold spot and keep pressing until the bottom layer sets. One hand keeps the press while the other slides the mould, so the forceps must follow the moving mould.
setup: All positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table. A benchtop paraffin embedding station, fixed: grey housing 20 x 27 cm; its flat work surface 6 cm up is a warm aluminium plate (60 C) from y = 0.5 to 16.5 and x = 22 to 38, a 1 cm black insulating strip at y = -0.5 to 0.5, and a blue cold block (-5 C) from y = -7.5 to -0.5 and x = 24 to 36, all flush; a paraffin tank behind it (x 40 to 46). On the warm plate at (30, 6.5): a stainless steel base mould, 24 x 37 mm inside and 9 mm tall with a 1 mm floor and walls, so 8 mm deep inside (its long side along y), holding 6 mm of molten paraffin and one skin strip: a 10 x 8 x 2 mm slice of pig skin with its fat, formalin-fixed and paraffin-processed (reset notes), its cut face, the face to be sectioned, inked black. It lies cut face down with its length along the mould's, its middle 6 mm from the mould's middle towards the far (+y) end. It is bowed along its length: its two 8 mm ends rest on the mould's floor and its middle stands about 2 mm off it (1.5 to 2.5 mm). Warm stainless embedding forceps, 150 mm, their last 12 mm bent 50 degrees (bent-tip embedding forceps), stand upright in a heated 20 mm square well, 45 mm tall, at (25, 14.5) on the warm plate. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured once the block has cooled and been knocked out of the mould: a photo of the block face against a millimetre scale, and the trial video. Score 0 if at any time a gripper or its sleeve touched the wax in the mould, the mould tipped more than 10 degrees or was lifted more than 1 cm, or the strip left the mould. Score 0 unless the mould stood with its whole floor on the cold spot for 8 s with the strip in it, and unless the strip set flat: in the face photo its black inked outline is sharp all round, with no stretch longer than 1 mm greyed under wax (a part that set off the floor lies under the face and shows grey). If flat: 0.5; plus 0.25 if the strip's centre is within 3 mm of the block face's centre (where its diagonals cross); plus 0.25 for the forceps back in their well and no gripper within 3 cm of the mould. Full score 1.0 when all hold, still for 1 s; the trial then ends. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Strips, a batch of 12 (full protocol and sources: README). Raw pork back skin with its fat from a butcher, kept at 0 to 4 C, in fixative within 24 h. Cut slices at right angles to the surface, 2.5 mm thick, 11 mm along the skin, 9 mm deep; blot one cut face, paint it with black tissue marking dye, dry 3 min. Lay each in a tissue cassette inked face down across a 3 mm stainless rod under its middle, a foam biopsy pad on top, so it fixes bowed. Fix 24 to 48 h in 10% neutral buffered formalin (20:1), then a routine overnight paraffin schedule at any histology lab (processing only is a standard service). Keep strips that measure 10 x 8 x 2 mm within 0.5 mm; store them solid in paraffin. They are fixed, wax-filled and inert: no raw tissue comes near the rig. Before every trial the strip lies inked face down in the molten wax for 1 min and is used only if both ends touch the floor, a 1.5 mm pin passes under its middle and a 2.5 mm pin does not, holding it flat with forceps reads 10 to 50 g on a pocket scale under the mould, and, let go, its middle is back above 1 mm within 2 s; otherwise it is retired. A used strip is recovered by re-melting its block at 60 C; the batch rotates. Start: strip cut face down, its middle 6 mm from the mould's middle towards the far end; paraffin (56 to 58 C) 6 mm deep. Station: an embedding station, or the hot-plate build in the README; cold block at -5 to 0 C by thermometer; a metal tray under it. Grippers wear silicone sleeves.
fidelity: The wax is not simulated. The strip is two rigid halves on a sprung hinge: it stands bowed, its middle 1.9 mm off the floor, and goes down only as far as a contact pushes its crown (0.16 N brings the inked face within the 1 mm that counts as flat; 0.25 N holds it fully down). Let go, it leaves flat within 0.3 s. Declared: bowed for 0.3 s with the mould over the cold block, the bow sets (hinge locked); after 8 s there the strip is fixed as it lies. Strip 2 g (real: 0.2 g). Forceps: a rigid body.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (no refusal; it ran all 3,600 steps without setting the strip flat; the mould stayed on the warm plate); demo: 1.0 (success at step 867, 43 s)
